assumptions: Assignments are permutations with hard one-per-row and one-per-column constraints.
The target is μ(π) proportional to exp(hᵀz(π)+½‖Bz(π)‖²), with explicit B or a factor whose construction/evaluation costs are charged.
A computable field region D passes the reported covariance and Gaussian-tail certificate: δ<1 and θ<1.
The theorem is stated in real arithmetic; the reported implementation is floating point.

costs.benchmark_scope: Reported transposition baselines were faster in all four generic matched cases. These effective-sample estimates are diagnostics, not convergence proofs or speedup evidence.
costs.certificate: Compute κ≥‖BᵀB‖op, d≥max diagonal, M≥max over cells and permutations of |h_e+(Kz)_e|, choose L>M; the source gives linear-assignment or cheaper sufficient ways to bound M.
costs.gap: R=exp(2L), δ=2n²exp(−(L−M)²/(2d)), θ=2R²(1+R²)κ/n; if both <1, γ≥(1−δ)(1−θ).
costs.initialization: If no cheap initial draw is available, solve a linear assignment maximizing hᵀz; the reported target-mass lower bound is exp(−nκ/2)/n! and the report gives a corresponding burn-in formula. Bounded-initial-field cases omit ½log(n!).
costs.inner_draw: Huber–Law nesting rejection; reported expected arithmetic cost O(R n² log(n+2)+A_R n^((R²+3)/2)); for fixed L≤1/3 the exponent is ≤3.396834. No permanent oracle is used.
costs.other_costs: The report also charges input/factor storage, certificate construction, Gaussian generation, matrix products, precision, and reports O(rn²) storage plus O(rn⁴) for the simple generic M bound. Its Fourier factor uses O(n²) for Bz and O(n²log n) for Bᵀy.

contract.interface: Draw Y|z~N(Bz,I); if Y∈D draw an explicit weighted permutation from the induced linear field, otherwise hold at z. The guarded kernel preserves the target; a finite run is approximate and uses the spectral-gap bound.
